{{Short description|Australian entomologist (1940–2024)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=August 2024}}{{Use Australian English|date=May 2024}}

'''Elizabeth A. Bernays''' (1940<ref>{{Cite web |title=VIAF ID 93683213 |url=https://viaf.org/viaf/93683213/ |access-date=2024-05-13 |website=VIAF}}</ref> – 5 March 2024) was an Australian entomologist who was a Regents Professor at the [[University of Arizona]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Garvey |first=Kathy Keatley |date=25 March 2024 |title=In Remembrance: Entomologists Charles Mitter, Elizabeth Bernays and Kim Flottum |url=https://entomology.ucdavis.edu/news/memorials |access-date=12 May 2024 |website=UC Davis Department of Entomology and Nematology website}}</ref> She was known for studies of physiological, behavioural, and ecological interactions between plants, herbivorous insects and their predators. Bernays worked on the feeding behaviour of a variety of insects including [[Aphid|aphids]], [[Grasshopper|grasshoppers]], and [[Sphingidae|hawkmoths]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bernays |first1=Elizabeth A. |last2=Funk |first2=Daniel J. |date=1999 |title=Specialists make faster decisions than generalists: experiments with aphids |url=https://doi.org/10.1098/rspb.1999.0615 |journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society of London B |volume=266 |issue=1415 |pages=151–156|doi=10.1098/rspb.1999.0615 |pmc=1689657 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Copenhaver |first=Larry |date=18 December 1990 |title=Pet project: Marvelous munching Menlanoplus excite, sadden students |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/578571605 |access-date=12 May 2024 |work=Tucson Citizen |pages=C1}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Espelie |first1=K.S. |last2=Bernays |first2=E.A. |date=1989 |title=Diet-related differences in the cuticular lipids of Manduca sexta larvar |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01207433 |journal=Journal of Chemical Ecology |volume=15 |issue=7 |pages=2003–2017|doi=10.1007/BF01207433 |pmid=24272291 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> She was known for championing the idea that predation drove many insects to specialise on a few species of hostplants, rather than specialisation being solely the outcome of a chemical arms race between plant and insect herbivores.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Mira |first1=Alex |last2=Bernays |first2=Elizabeth A. |date=2002 |title=Tradeoffs in host use by Manduca sexta: plant characters versus natural enemies |journal=Oikos |volume=97 |pages=387–397|doi=10.1034/j.1600-0706.2002.970309.x }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Frederick |first=Donald J. |date=5 September 1993 |title=Potent ocean poisons could help fight diseases on land |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/712028678 |access-date=12 May 2024 |work=Los Angeles Times |pages=A10}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Minard |first=Anne |date=19 January 2005 |title=The writing bug has captured scientist |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/221509744 |access-date=12 May 2024 |work=Arizona Daily Star |pages=B1–B2}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Educated at the [[University of Queensland]], Australia, she moved to London to teach high school students; she subsequently studied for a PhD there.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Bernays |first=Elizabeth A. |date=2019 |title=An Unlikely Beginning: A Fortunate Life |url=https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-ento-011118-111820 |journal=Annual Review of Entomology |volume=64 |pages=1–13|doi=10.1146/annurev-ento-011118-111820 |pmid=30629895 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> Prior to moving to the University of Arizona, she was a professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name=":0" />   

== Career ==
Bernays published more than 100 book chapters, peer-reviewed journal articles, edited volumes and books on a variety of entomological subjects including insect learning, feeding, taste and water homeostasis.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Reuven |first1=Dukas |last2=Bernays |first2=Elizabeth A |date=2000 |title=Learning improves growth rate in grasshoppers |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |volume=97 |pages=2637–26|doi=10.1073/pnas.05046149 |doi-broken-date=12 July 2025 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Reisenman |first1=Carolina E. |last2=Riffell |first2=Jeffrey A. |last3=Bernays |first3=Elizabeth A. |last4=Hildebrand |first4=John A. |date=2010 |title=Antagonistic effects of floral scent in an insect–plant interaction |url=https://doi.org/10.1098/rspb.2010.0163 |journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society B |volume=277 |issue=1692 |pages=2371–2379|doi=10.1098/rspb.2010.0163 |pmid=20335210 |pmc=2894902 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Woods |first1=H. Arthur |last2=Bernays |first2=Elizabeth A. |date=2001 |title=Water homeostasis by wild larvae of Manduca sexta |url=https://doi.org/10.1046/j.1365-3032.2000.00167.x |journal=Physiological Entomology |volume=25 |pages=82–87|doi=10.1046/j.1365-3032.2000.00167.x |url-access=subscription }}</ref> Her research into the feeding behaviour of insects helped guide interventions designed to minimise crop pest damage.<ref name=":1" /> Along with Michael S. Singer, she published a paper in 2005 in ''Nature'' showing that parasitised tiger moth caterpillars have greater sensitivity to [[Pyrrolizidine alkaloid|pyrrolizidine alkaloids]] than non-parasitised caterpillars and that parasitised caterpillars seek out plants containing these chemicals to defend themselves from predation and parasitism.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bernays |first1=Elizabeth A. |last2=Singer |first2=Michael S. |date=2005 |title=Taste alteration and endoparasites |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/436476a |journal=Nature |volume=436 |issue=7050 |pages=476|doi=10.1038/436476a |pmid=16049466 |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Hathaway |first=William |date=1 August 2005 |title=Insect eats to fight what ails it |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/192769237 |url-status= |access-date=12 May 2024 |work=Los Angeles Times |pages=F6}}</ref>

== Academic honours ==
In 1986, she received the Vatican's highest scientific honour, the [[Pius XI Gold Medal]] of the [[Pontifical Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=13 September 1986 |title=Berkeley Professor Honored by Vatican |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/404659950 |work=Los Angeles Times |pages=19}}</ref>
== Late career activities ==
After retirement, Bernays studied for a master's degree in creative writing at the University of Arizona.<ref name=":0" /> She wrote two memoirs''.'' The first memoir, ''Six Legs Walking: Notes from an Entomological Live,'' described her childhood experiences with nature, her work with her husband as an applied entomologist in Africa, and her professional experiences as a woman in science moving from the science culture of the U.K. to a professorship at the University of California, Berkeley.<ref>{{Cite news |date=1 May 2022 |title=Local authors cover wide range of topics |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/837583775 |access-date=12 May 2024 |work=Arizona Daily Star |pages=E2}}</ref> Her second memoir, ''Across the Divide: The Strangest Love Affair,'' describes her personal and creative relationship with her wife Linda Hitchcock which included collaborating on children's nature books and travelling the southwestern U.S.<ref>{{Cite news |date=3 September 2023 |title=Poems, memoirs, history and mysteries |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1000972194 |access-date=12 May 2024 |work=Arizona Daily Star |pages=E7}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
She was married to the English entomologist [[Reginald Frederick Chapman]] until his death in 2003. She met Linda Hitchcock, photojournalist in 2004 and subsequently married  in 2018  .

== Selected books and edited volumes ==
* ''Herbivores and Plant Tannins'' with Gillian A. Cooper-Driver and M. Bilgener, London: Academic Press, 1989.
* ''Insect-Plant Interactions,'' Boca Raton: CRC Press, 1990.
* ''Host-Plant Selection by Phytophagous Insects'' with R.F. Chapman, New York: Chapman & Hall, 1994.
* ''Six Legs Walking: Notes from an Entomological Life'', Florida: Raised Voices Press, 2019.
* ''Across the Divide: The Strangest Love Affair,'' Arizona: Wheatmark, 2023.
